1. Aim & Objectives

To design, implement, and deploy a fully scalable, event-driven Serverless Feedback Management Application on Amazon Web Services (AWS) that allows students to submit course feedback and retrieve previously submitted feedback using RESTful APIs, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB.

2. Architecture Overview

Client (Curl/Postman) ──► Amazon API Gateway (/feedback) ──► AWS Lambda (Python 3.11) ──► Amazon DynamoDB (FeedbackDB)
  - POST /feedback: Submits feedback payload & stores into DynamoDB
  - GET  /feedback/: Fetches feedback item by FeedbackID from DynamoDB

3. Step 1: Create DynamoDB Table (FeedbackDB)

Created a DynamoDB table named FeedbackDB with FeedbackID (String) as the Partition Key. Table status verified as Active.

Figure 1: DynamoDB Table 'FeedbackDB' created with Partition Key FeedbackID (Active).

4. Step 2: IAM Role Configuration

Configured an IAM Execution Role with AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess and AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole policies to allow the Lambda functions to execute read/write operations on DynamoDB.

Figure 2: IAM Role with AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess policy successfully attached.

5. Step 3 & 4: Implement Submit Feedback Lambda (SubmitFeedback)

Implemented Lambda function in Python 3.11 to parse student feedback submissions (FeedbackID, StudentName, CourseName, Rating, Comments) and store them in DynamoDB via put_item().

Figure 3: SubmitFeedback Lambda function code deployed successfully.

6. Step 5: Implement Retrieve Feedback Lambda (GetFeedback)

Created a second Lambda function in Python 3.11 to retrieve feedback details by path parameter /feedback/ using get_item() with automatic Decimal type serialization for JSON responses.

Figure 4: Function GetFeedback created successfully.
Figure 5: GetFeedback Lambda code updated and deployed.

7. Step 6, 7 & 8: Build Amazon API Gateway & Integrate with Lambda

Created REST API named FeedbackAPI. Configured endpoints:

  • POST /feedback: Integrated with SubmitFeedback (Lambda Proxy Integration enabled)
  • GET /feedback/: Integrated with GetFeedback (Lambda Proxy Integration enabled)
Figure 6: REST API 'FeedbackAPI' created.
Figure 7: Endpoints POST /feedback and GET /feedback/{id} configured.

8. Step 9: Deploy API to Stage 'dev'

The API was deployed to a stage named dev, generating the active Invoke URL: https://jp36f93rp8.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/dev.

Figure 8: FeedbackAPI deployed to stage 'dev' with active Invoke URL.

9. Step 10: Endpoint Testing & JSON Responses

A. Submit Feedback Test (POST /feedback)

curl -X POST https://jp36f93rp8.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/dev/feedback \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"FeedbackID": "FB101", "StudentName": "Ayush Singh", "CourseName": "SOA", "Rating": 5, "Comments": "Great course and practical lab!"}'

Response (HTTP 201 Created):
{"message": "Feedback submitted successfully!", "data": {"FeedbackID": "FB101", "StudentName": "Ayush Singh", "CourseName": "SOA", "Rating": 5, "Comments": "Great course and practical lab!"}}

B. Retrieve Feedback Test (GET /feedback/FB101)

curl -X GET https://jp36f93rp8.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/dev/feedback/FB101

Response (HTTP 200 OK):
{"StudentName": "Ayush Singh", "Comments": "Great course and practical lab!", "CourseName": "SOA", "Rating": 5, "FeedbackID": "FB101"}
